cards.title: Culture of 'ideal' childbirth needs to evolve
cards.body: Letters respond to an article about a five-day labour, with an NHS doctor sharing her experience of feeling 'othered' by childbirth culture. The discussion highlights how societal expectations around labour need to change.

cards.title: Second baby has made me forget everything
cards.body: New parent reflects on how much she's forgotten since her first child—from feeding to teething to everything in between. Her mum's practical help has stirred memories of her own blissfully bored childhood.

cards.title: Should AI help with parenting decisions?
cards.body: Tech companies now offer eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts, and 'optimized nap predictions' for parents. The article questions whether busy parents actually need these tools.

cards.title: '18 summers' parenting trend: skip it
cards.body: Long, unstructured summer days are the whole point—turning them into a 'making memories' exercise is creepy and controlling. Modern parenting trends often miss the value of boredom.

cards.title: Family games night as kids grow up
cards.body: One parent reflects on hosting a final family games night as their 20-year era of five living together comes to an end. The evening becomes a bittersweet memory of changing family dynamics.

cards.title: Young adults trapped at home by economics
cards.body: More UK young people live with parents as low wages, insecure work, and unaffordable housing make independence impossible. Family support has become another source of inequality.

cards.title: Back-to-school emotional weight on parents
cards.body: Parents are doing far more than buying supplies—they're carrying the emotional burden of wanting children to feel they belong. Back-to-school season amplifies parental anxiety and expectations.

cards.title: AI therapists may appeal to next generation
cards.body: Today's adults may resist AI therapy, but children raised with AI will have no resistance to tools they grew up with. The acceptance gap between generations could reshape mental health support.

cards.title: Fanfiction writing benefits children's development
cards.body: When fans use AI to write fanfiction instead of creating their own, children lose valuable benefits of imaginary play and expressive writing. Handwritten storytelling remains crucial practice for young writers.

cards.title: Anxiety can pass from parent to child
cards.body: Your anxiety may be teaching your child to be anxious too through how you respond to fear. Small changes in parental reactions can break the anxiety cycle and build children's confidence.

cards.title: ADHD burnout in kids and teens warning signs
cards.body: Children struggling more than usual with motivation or emotions may be experiencing ADHD burnout, not just typical ADHD symptoms. Understanding burnout signs helps parents provide proper support.

cards.title: Postpartum psychosis hides behind common symptoms
cards.body: Postpartum psychosis can masquerade as anxiety, insomnia, and depression, making it dangerous to miss. Recognizing its shifting symptoms can be lifesaving for new mothers.

cards.title: Mothers' darkest postpartum thoughts need safe spaces
cards.body: Creating safe spaces for mothers to share their darkest postpartum thoughts can be part of recovery. Hidden shame often prevents parents from seeking help when struggling most.

cards.title: When adult children's crises become your life
cards.body: You can love your adult child deeply without living on permanent high alert by being in emotional standby. Setting boundaries protects both parent and child.

cards.title: Mindfulness works for emotionally neglected people
cards.body: A psychologist who once dismissed mindfulness explains why it feels impossible for emotionally neglected people, then offers a simple exercise that makes it work. Early childhood experiences shape adult mindfulness capacity.

cards.title: Intelligence matters more than just IQ
cards.body: Not all kinds of intelligence can be measured on standardized tests. Parents should recognize their children's varied strengths beyond academic metrics.

cards.title: Sleep strategies for parents and children
cards.body: Consider these strategies to create conditions for your nervous system to find its way into sleep. Good sleep habits benefit both parents managing stress and children developing healthy patterns.
